title: Andy Schectman: I’ve Been Buying Gold Every 2 Weeks
speaker: Andy Schectman

macro_themes.view: Record gold/silver standing for delivery shows sophisticated buyers (possibly Treasury proxies or Tether) accumulating physical metal while paper prices are suppressed.
Paper-market weakness is being used to transfer metal from weak to strong hands; not a genuine collapse in demand.
Countries are repatriating gold and building non-Western payment systems, using gold instead of Treasuries.
Retail is all-in on ~10 stocks with record margin and option exposure; most S&P stocks are down ~20%, a fragile setup.
Judy Shelton's appointment to Bessent's advisory council is more than a coincidence and signals gold moving back into monetary policy.

calls.reason: The ~30% drop from $5,500-5,600 was the correction; central banks, China and COMEX delivery takers keep accumulating regardless of price, so he doesn't expect further falls.
calls.quote: Question is, does it continue to fall? I don't think so. The physical demand is too strong.

calls.reason: Silver is down over 50% but fundamentals are unchanged: ongoing deficit, record Chinese imports, ~$18B delivered on COMEX this year; big money is accumulating at suppressed prices.
calls.quote: Of course. I mean mathematically there's tremendous potential... it stings, but nothing has really changed.

calls.reason: Mining, rare-earth and resource stocks are an undervalued, unloved segment as countries race to secure strategic metals and energy.
calls.quote: I buy mining shares and and natural resource stocks, which I believe where we are heading represent a true undervalued segment

notes: Gold price_at_call 4100 is the host's quote ('4,100 / $4,000'), not the guest's. Gold medium-term bias inferred from 'does it continue to fall? I don't think so'. Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) mentioned only as a long-held position that did well; skipped. Miners mapped to GDX though he talks about resource stocks broadly. Contains conference promo.
